what_it_does: Multi-task learning trains a single model to perform multiple related tasks (e.g., detecting and classifying objects simultaneously). On mobile and embedded devices, this must balance three competing goals: high accuracy on each task, low parameter count (to fit in memory), and fast inference (low latency). Most existing multi-task learning methods focus on accuracy and model size but ignore latency constraints during search, requiring manual tuning afterward that often compromises performance. LA-MTL (Latency-Aware Automated Multi-Task Learning) integrates latency directly into the architecture search using a novel Analytical Latency Factor (ALF) that predicts both per-layer and end-to-end inference time. The search explores different ways to share layers across tasks, using ALF to guide the process toward Pareto-optimal solutions that balance accuracy, efficiency, and latency without post-hoc tuning.
